newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Thousands attend emotional burial of Greek Cypriot.
newsitem.headline: Thousands attend emotional burial of Greek Cypriot.

text.p: About 3,000 Cypriots on Tuesday attended an emotionally charged funeral to bury a Greek Cypriot man shot dead by Turkish Cypriot troops on Sunday.
Retired Greek Cypriot fireman Petros Kakouli, 58, was lowered to his grave in a wooden coffin draped with the Greek flag in the southeast village of Avgorou.

Turkish Cypriot troops shot him dead when he entered Turkish-occupied territory on Sunday morning. His family said he was in the area collecting snails. Turkish forces said he failed to stop when ordered to by troops and was shot whilst escaping.

The incident, which the United Nations peacekeeping force on the island described as "deplorable", happened near the eastern end of the buffer zone, close to Achna village and territory controlled by British military bases.
The funeral was highly charged. One of Kakouli's two daughters, Martha, collapsed and was rushed out of church screaming. She was given oxygen and put in an ambulance.
Cypriot Finance Minister Christodoulos Christodoulou told a packed church that the killing of Kakouli was an "abhorrent murder".

"The bullets of the killers of the ruthless Attila cut your life short. Your ruthless killers tried to continue the crimes they committed in August," he said, referring to two Greek Cypriot youths killed during protests against division of the island in the U.N. buffer zone,
Four Greek Cypriots and one Turkish Cypriot have been killed along the buffer zone since June.

U.N. officials said security has been stepped up along the buffer zone dividing the island for the funeral. British soldiers from a nearby British base on the island patrolled in jeeps on a road leading to the village.
"The order is to be extremely vigilant," U.N. spokesman Waldemar Rokoszewski said.
Groups of Greek Cypriot students demonstrated along the "green line" dividing the capital Nicosia on Tuesday, shortly before the funeral.

Secondary school students gathered at the United Nations- controlled Ledra Palace checkpoint chanting "Our borders are in Kyrenia" but quickly dispersed. Other students held protests in schoolyards. Some 200 to 300 took part in total.
Kyrenia, on the north coast of Cyprus, has been occupied by Turkish forces since 1974 when Turkey invaded the northern third of the island in response to a Greek-engineered coup in Nicosia.
A Turkish Cypriot breakaway state in the north, recognised only by Ankara, was established in 1983.
